action_summary: Two claims were computed from a lookup key instead of from the artifact, one layer apart, and both were certified. (1) The door classified an adapter refusal by the EXCEPTION CLASS it arrived in -- SystemExit(json) parsed, RuntimeError("GUARD_KEY:detail") not -- so 7 of the 13 refusals in the 49-sentence advanced census came back FAIL__LIVE_CONTROLLER_EXECUTION, the status of an adapter bug, with the cause the exception already named discarded (POLYGLOT_REFUSED:CPP_NO_APPLICABLE_TRANSFORM x2, SQL_UNSUPPORTED_DDL_EDIT, PYPROJECT_ALREADY_PINNED_OR_EMPTY, NO_DECLARED_DEPENDENCY_TO_VENDOR, NO_FLAKY_TEST_DETECTED, TARGET_SYMBOL_COLLISION:add). (2) The dependency audit classified a package by its NAME: membership in a six-entry advisory dict was the whole test, so requests==2.32.3, pyyaml==6.0.1 and cryptography==43.0.0 -- all past their fixes -- were reported vulnerable and the door stamped exact semantic acceptance over the report. Both now read the artifact: the refusal keeps its own key, and the audit compares the pinned version to the fixed version and names what it could not judge.
